items.title: What can university recruitment and teaching preparation verify?

values: Materials and setup｜T1—T4 are all editorially fictional

T1｜Learning objectives: after completing the ten-minute lesson, a fictional learner can calculate the pass rates of two groups, describe the difference in percentage points, distinguish description from causation and identify one specific design limitation. Do a paper or self-reported exercise only, without contacting real people, recruiting students or evaluating real grades.

T2｜Fictional case: group A has 10 people, of whom 6 passed; group B has 10 people, of whom 8 passed. The two groups are not randomly assigned, and baseline levels, other condition controls or pre-post measurement are not given. No new facts may be added, and it cannot be said that B's teaching method is proven more effective.

T3｜Three independent fictional answers: A “6/10=60%, 8/10=80%, B is 20 percentage points higher, so B's method caused the higher pass rate”; B “60% and 80%, a difference of 20 percentage points; the groups are not random and student baselines may differ, so the method cannot be proven to cause the difference”; C “60% and 80%, B is a 20% relative increase; the sample is small, so the conclusion should be cautious”. A, B and C are not any real students.

T4｜Four 1-point rubric items: both group proportions are correct; the difference is explicitly written as 20 percentage points; it is explicitly stated that the teaching method's causal effect cannot be proven from this; at least one specific limitation such as non-random assignment, possibly different baselines or a small sample is identified. The items are independent, and bases not explicitly written may not be added for the answer; the total is 0—4 and assesses the given fictional text only.

Lesson timing｜2 minutes explaining proportions and percentage points; 3 minutes reading T2 and recalculating; 3 minutes discussing “can the difference prove an effect”; 2 minutes for the exit question and feedback, 10 minutes in total. The arrangement is an editorial example only and does not claim to have been verified in a classroom.

Work product requirements｜Submit four work products: the ten-minute lesson plan, the T2 case and exit question materials, the item-by-item scoring sheet for A, B and C, and one specific feedback and revision note per answer. Seal the lesson plan and scoring independently before checking the answers; a position, wording preference or guess may not replace the rubric.
Tasks and outputs

Organize the ten-minute lesson around the T1 objectives, with an exit question requiring both group proportions, the percentage point difference and the causal boundary. Score A, B and C item by item as 0 or 1 according to T4, write the textual basis and total the scores.

Submit the four work products plus the independent first draft and revisions; feedback identifies specific missing items and how to fix them, and the total score is not treated as a real person's academic ability or a hiring conclusion.
Reference answers (finish independently first, then check)

A's pass rate is 6/10=60% and B's is 8/10=80%; B minus A = 20 percentage points. The relative increase is (80−60)/60 ≈ 33.3%, so C's explicit statement of “a 20% relative increase” is incorrect. With non-random groups and no baseline control, the teaching method's causal effect cannot be proven.

Scoring in the order of the four items: A 1/1/0/0 for a total of 2; B 1/1/1/1 for a total of 4; C 1/0/0/1 for a total of 2. A's causal assertion fails the third item and states no specific limitation; C's mention of a small sample satisfies the fourth item, but the causal denial and the correct percentage points cannot be added on C's behalf.

Feedback example: A keeps the calculation and deletes the causal assertion and writes non-random and other limitations; B keeps the complete explanation and may further state what design evidence is needed; C changes the 20% relative figure to a difference of 20 percentage points and states clearly that the method effect cannot be proven. Feedback matches the missing items and gives no real person's grade.
Boundaries and review

T1—T4, the two groups and the three answers are all fictional; the rubric is an editorial exercise, not a school examination rule or a validated ability scale. Real teaching, evaluation, student materials and appeal review are handled according to credential appointment and school duties; no real personal materials are collected or modified.

paragraphs: The BLS typical entry for this occupation in the United States is a doctoral or professional degree; the O*NET new hire figures of 77% doctoral and 23% master's are U.S. occupational data, not Chinese legal education or a uniform employer condition. Both teaching-focused and combined teaching and research positions fall within this category.

China's Teachers Law college credential education condition includes graduate or undergraduate study, with other conditions and application for recognition also required. The teaching credential regulations list the college category separately, and school-level credentials are not directly mutually recognized for colleges. Article 9 of the implementation measures handles some conditions differently for applicants to be appointed as an associate professor or higher, or applicants with a doctorate, but character, education, physical condition and recognition still apply; this is not automatic certification or exemption from all procedures. The competent department's or authorized college's current materials and process are verified separately.

The Shanghai University sociology team posting lists professor, associate professor and lecturer, requires a doctorate and covers teaching, research and public service responsibility; the Peking University 2026 sociology department posting includes different pre-tenure and tenure levels and requires a doctorate and English teaching. These two employer samples cannot be extrapolated to the threshold, wages or promotion of all Chinese universities.

The BLS all-postsecondary-teacher background notes that academic appointments may combine research, teaching and institutional contribution evaluation; U.S. tenure, Chinese titles, public institution posts, pre-tenure and tenure are not a single mutually recognized system. Term, class hours, research review, guidance and exit conditions are verified against the complete contract, with no fixed-year automatic promotion promised.

description.text: Teach sociology courses at colleges and universities, design course materials, organize discussion, evaluate student work, and may also take on research publication, guidance and departmental service. The balance of teaching-focused and teaching-research positions, terms and review differ. This page uses fictional scores for two groups and three answers to practice a ten-minute micro-lesson and a scoring rubric, without contacting real students or replacing teaching credential recognition.
